title.value: Temporal Abstractions-Augmented Temporally Contrastive Learning: An Alternative to the Laplacian in RL
title.justification: The title accurately captures the primary focus of the paper, which is to present an alternative method to the Laplacian in reinforcement learning through temporal abstractions augmented temporally contrastive learning.
title.quote: T EMPORAL ABSTRACTIONS - AUGMENTED TEMPORALLY CONTRASTIVE LEARNING : AN ALTERNATIVE TO THE L APLACIAN IN RL

extractions.description: This paper introduces a new approach in reinforcement learning called Temporal Abstractions-augmented Temporally Contrastive learning (TATC). TATC integrates temporal abstractions into the representation learning process to address challenges related to exploration in non-uniform prior settings. The paper argues that this method improves upon traditional Laplacian-based methods by offering a more effective training distribution through a skill-based covering policy, leading to better representation quality and dynamics-awareness in challenging continuous navigation tasks with sparse rewards.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on reinforcement learning techniques for solving representation learning and exploration challenges in RL, particularly compared to Laplacian methods. While these advancements have the potential to impact various fields, the paper doesn't explicitly connect to any central eco-responsible category or application.
primary_category.quote: In reinforcement learning (RL), the graph Laplacian has proved to be a valuable tool in the task-agnostic setting, with applications ranging from option discovery to dynamics-aware metric learning.

primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a representation learning framework that conciliate a similar temporally-contrastive approach with exploration in the task-agnostic setting.
